outcome: cervical dilation prior to CD for failure to progress
cohort: Pregnant women planning a vaginal birth who had a live, singleton delivery from January 2015 to December 2018, consisting of Class III obese (BMI >=40 kg/m(2)) and normal BMI (BMI <25 kg/m(2)) women matched 1:1 based on age, gestational age, parity, onset of labour and birth weight.
finding: Class III obesity is associated with an increased risk of caesarean delivery and higher rates of intrapartum interventions.
mod_finding: The caesarean delivery rate was significantly higher for obese women (19.3%) compared to the normal BMI cohort (13.3%), with a risk ratio of 1.43.
birth_weight: Matching criterion; specific range not provided.
gest_age: Matching criterion; specific range not provided.
